name: Antioch earthquake
summary: A magnitude-7 earthquake on 20 May 526 destroys most of Antioch on the Orontes, with chronicled casualty estimates of 250,000 (almost certainly inflated). A second major shock follows in 528. Justin I and Justinian fund extensive reconstruction, but the city's late-antique demographic peak is never recovered.

_quarry.structural_significance: Demographic and economic blow to the Late-Antique Levant on the eve of the Persian-Byzantine wars and the Justinianic Plague; combined with these, marks the structural decline of Antioch from third-city of the empire to a regional town.
